# RCS Day 7 - Integrated Wall Build: Correct, Complete, Prove
CTS Cohort 6 | CTS Day 15 | 2026-07-29 | 10:00 AM-3:00 PM

## Core rule
A professional does not guess. A professional checks, protects, and verifies.

## Big idea
Integration means every system fits, remains inspectable, and can be explained with evidence - not merely that the wall looks finished.

## Architecture of the day
| Time | Instructor move |
|---|---|
| 10:00-10:15 | Arrival, PPE, retrieval warm-up |
| 10:15-10:30 | Morning quiz |
| 10:30-10:50 | Quiz review and whole-wall QC frame |
| 10:50-11:20 | Subsystem and whole-wall inspection model |
| 11:20-12:00 | Punch-list and acceptance-criteria practice |
| 12:00-12:30 | Handoff evidence model and rework release |
| 12:30-1:00 | Lunch and controlled reset |
| 1:00-2:25 | Approved rework and capstone completion lab |
| 2:25-2:45 | Retest, whole-wall QC, handoff practice, cleanup |
| 2:45-3:00 | Exit ticket and final-practical preview |

## Learning targets
- Complete remaining capstone framing, electrical, and drywall work
- Run a subsystem and whole-wall QC inspection
- Diagnose and correct one documented defect
- Prepare a professional handoff package

## Materials and setup
- Six capstone walls and current subsystem drawings
- Whole-wall QC checklists, punch-list forms, and acceptance criteria
- Task-specific hand tools and isolated electrical test equipment under prior controls
- Labels, evidence file-name plan, and approved cameras/devices
- Rework-zone barriers and cleanup materials
- Handoff rubric and 60-second timer

## Instructor talking points
- Define system-level versus whole-project inspection.
- Model a punch list that names location, expected condition, observed condition, corrective action, and verification.
- Review all energy boundaries before students reopen device boxes or change wiring.
- Demonstrate evidence photos: overall, detail, test setup, and corrected result.
- Explain that honest documentation includes unresolved items rather than hiding them.
